propertyEvents.result: The FY2025 reserve, $118,000.00, reversed on July 1, 2025 with last year’s other accruals; the year’s warranty work was charged to job costs as it was done. The June 30, 2026 reserve is the Controller’s schedule: $125,000.00 for the 6 jobs completed in FY2026, job by job, the same as entry 26-01257 (AJ-26-0635) and the accruals schedule. Every warranty runs a year from completion, the last to June 12, 2027. The largest, $36,000.00, is Kestrel Point Hotel; Corliss, finished at a loss and in dispute, carries $20,000.00. The CPA judges the estimate (EST-01).

log.text: The bank confirmed $5,554,191.74 for the operating account ending 4471 directly, the same as its June statement. 6 checks written in June, $122,451.49, are not on it, and the statement’s May 31 balance is $70,054.94 above the ledger’s: checks written earlier, still out. The cash audit names them, two May checks that cleared in July and check 21561 of December 18, 2025, never presented (STALE-01). Taking them off leaves $5,361,685.31, the ledger’s operating cash. The payroll account ending 6158: $168,915.40 per the bank against $172,980.40, the bank’s $4,065.00 of charges never recorded (FEE-01, clearly trivial). The June 30 dividend left by wire that day ($90,000.00). The bank confirms the term loan, $2,880,000.00, and the line, $1,800,000.00, the trial balance’s, with $28,665.00 of June interest accrued and debited July 1 that the books do not hold (UL-04).

log.text: Contract revenue rose from $59,356,800.00 to $68,989,500.00 (16.2%) and the gross margin from 5.7% to 10.1%, in line with the job margins the work in progress testing recomputed. FY2025 ended in a loss of $2,712,576.39; FY2026 earned $1,125,090.40, a swing of $3,837,666.79 the CPA should understand from last year’s file. General and administrative costs fell from $5,791,017.39 to $5,516,004.50. By month: interest expense is 24 bank debits for the 12 months June 2025 to May 2026, so the year carries last June’s interest and not this June’s, $28,665.00 (UL-04). Questions for management and judgments for the CPA.

Add up what every area found and set it against materiality

Known misstatements add up to $559,962.23 of FY2026 income: this run’s TOP-01 ($48,000.00) and UL-01 to UL-04 ($247,985.00), and the other areas’ WIP-01, AR-01, SE-01, SE-02, ACC-01, FEE-01 and the equipment audit’s net, $263,977.23, each as its area added it up. That is 164.7% of materiality: left unrecorded, the statements would be materially misstated, so the CPA asks management to record them. If the CPA accepts CROSS-01, Pier 9 revenue at cost-to-cost once UL-01 is recorded ($204,835.16), the total is $355,127.07, still above materiality. INV-01 ($840.00) is clearly trivial and listed, not added up; AFF-01 ($7,891.34), EST-01 and the unread invoice wait for a person. The balance sheet also leaves out $2,100,383.96 of lease liabilities (the equipment audit). June 30 tangible net worth is $497,195.07 above the loan agreement’s minimum before any of these (the covenant procedures): recorded in full they would take it $62,767.16 below; net of CROSS-01 it stays $142,068.00 above, so covenant compliance at June 30 depends on what management records (COV-01). Comparing the totals with materiality and concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.
